tip: Stand the cilantro stems in a glass of water in the fridge and it will stay usable for over a week.

pkg: Small flat rectangular pack with a clear front, showing paper-thin rosy-pink slices layered with sheets of film between them, in the deli case near the specialty cured meats.
look_for: The slices should be so thin you can almost see through them, with fine white fat running through the pink.
confuse: Pancetta cubes and thicker sliced Serrano-style ham sit in the same case and behave very differently in cooking.
tip: Peel the slices apart while they are still cold, as they tear once they warm up in your hands.

pkg: Clear-wrapped tray of one or two deep red steaks, sirloin being a broad lean slab and flat iron a narrower rectangle with a bright line of connective tissue down the middle.
look_for: Look for a steak at least three quarters of an inch thick so it can brown properly without overcooking inside.
confuse: Cube steak and thin sandwich steaks are cheaper and packed nearby but are pounded flat and will not sear the same way.
tip: Check the tray has no pooled liquid under the meat, which is a sign it has been sitting a while.

pkg: Tall glass bottle of thick glossy dark-brown sauce with a green or red cap, usually shelved with the soy and stir-fry sauces in the small international section.
look_for: The label should say oyster sauce or oyster-flavoured sauce and the contents should cling to the glass rather than slosh like soy sauce.
confuse: Soy sauce and hoisin sit right beside it, and soy sauce is thin and salty rather than thick and savoury-sweet.
tip: Aldi does not always carry this, so check the international aisle first and keep the bottle in the fridge once it is opened.

key: thick bone-in pork chops, about 1 1/2 lb total
pkg: Clear-wrapped tray holding two pale pink chops, each with a curved bone along one edge and a rim of white fat, standing noticeably taller than the thin chops beside them.
size: Around 1.5 lb total for two chops
look_for: Each chop should be about an inch or more thick, with the bone still attached and a good cap of fat on the outside edge.
confuse: The thin-cut boneless loin chops sit in the same section and cook in a fraction of the time.
tip: Thick chops benefit from resting a few minutes off the heat before you cut into them.

key: baharat or trader joe's 21 seasoning salute
display: Baharat or Trader Joe's 21 Seasoning Salute
pkg: Small clear plastic spice jar on the seasoning rack, the 21 Seasoning Salute showing a greenish-brown herb blend under a green-accented label with a shaker top.
look_for: Read the front carefully as Trader Joe's spice rack is packed with lookalike jars in the same shape and size.
confuse: Everything But The Bagel and the various chili-lime blends come in the same jar and are grabbed by mistake constantly.
tip: 21 Seasoning Salute has no salt in it, so season the dish separately rather than relying on the blend.

pkg: Small clear tub with a snap-on lid holding a vivid grassy-green herb paste, kept in the chilled case alongside the hummus and dips rather than on a shelf.
look_for: It should be bright green, coarse and spoonable, and the lid will read zhoug rather than pesto or chimichurri.
confuse: Basil pesto and the green cilantro dips in the same case look similar through the lid but taste nothing alike.
tip: It is properly spicy, so start with a small spoonful and stir it through before adding more.

key: season's choice frozen diced breakfast potatoes
display: Season's Choice Frozen Diced Breakfast Potatoes
pkg: Freezer bag with the green Season's Choice banner and a photo of golden potato cubes, often flecked with bits of red and green pepper and onion.
look_for: The front should say breakfast potatoes or potatoes with onions and peppers, not just plain diced potatoes.
confuse: The plain diced potatoes and the shredded hash browns share the same bag design a few inches away.
tip: Spread them in a single layer in a hot pan or oven and leave them alone so they crisp rather than steam.

pkg: Small resealable pouch, much smaller and pricier than the other nut bags, with the green Southern Grove logo and a photo of pale ivory teardrop-shaped kernels.
look_for: The kernels should be creamy ivory and uniform, and this is usually the smallest bag hanging in the nut section.
confuse: Slivered almonds and raw cashews are cheaper and sit alongside, but neither has the same soft resinous flavour.
tip: Pine nuts turn rancid fast, so store them in the freezer and toast them gently just before use.

pkg: Clear-wrapped tray of several flat pale pink ovals stacked or fanned out, all lean with no bone and only a thin strip of fat along one edge.
look_for: Look for chops roughly half an inch thick with no bone, so several fit in a pan at once.
confuse: The thick bone-in chops and the boneless loin roast are in the same case and need much longer cooking.
tip: These are very lean and go dry quickly, so sear them hot and fast and pull them off early.

pkg: Small flat foil-and-plastic pouch that stands up on the shelf, printed with a bowl of cooked rice and the Earthly Grains name, sold in single-serve sizes near the dry rice.
look_for: These are the ready-to-heat microwave pouches, so the front will advertise a cook time of a minute or two.
confuse: Boil-in-bag rice boxes sit on the same shelf but need a pot of water rather than a microwave.
tip: Squeeze the sealed pouch to break up the rice before you open or heat it and it will not come out in clumps.
